# Design

How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

---

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.
- Transactions: `govern: [ transaction ]` on steps, not `@Transactional`.
- Errors: a handler YAML in `officefloor/escalation/`, not `@ControllerAdvice`.

### Worked example — `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`

The whole shape of an endpoint. The sections after this one are the reference.

`src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml`

```yaml
# First step runs first. Validate before Load so an invalid body is a 400,
# not masked by a 404 for a missing owner.
validate:
  class: com.example.owner.ValidateOwner
  next: load
load:
  class: com.example.owner.LoadOwner
  next: apply
apply:
  class: com.example.owner.ApplyOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save
save:
  class: com.example.owner.SaveOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond
respond:
  class: com.example.owner.RespondWithOwner
```

```java
// One public method each. State moves by Out<T> (set) → @Val (read), matched by type.
public class ValidateOwner {
  public void validate(@RequestBody @Valid OwnerRequest request, Out<OwnerRequest> body) {
    body.set(request); // body read once here; republished for later steps
  }
}
public class LoadOwner {
  public void load(@PathVariable("ownerId") int ownerId, OwnerRepository repository,
      Out<Owner> ownerOut) throws OwnerNotFoundException {
    Owner owner = repository.findById(ownerId);
    if (owner == null) throw new OwnerNotFoundException(ownerId); // handled below
    ownerOut.set(owner);
  }
}
public class ApplyOwner { // @Val yields the stored object, not a copy — mutate in place
  public void apply(@Val OwnerRequest request, @Val Owner owner) {
    owner.setFirstName(request.firstName());
    owner.setLastName(request.lastName());
  }
}
public class SaveOwner {
  public void save(@Val Owner owner, OwnerRepository repository) {
    repository.save(owner);
  }
}
public class RespondWithOwner {
  public void respond(@Val Owner owner, ObjectResponse<OwnerResponse> response) {
    response.send(OwnerResponse.from(owner)); // this step responds; 200 by default
  }
}
```

`src/main/resources/officefloor/escalation/com.example.owner.OwnerNotFoundException.yml`

```yaml
handle:
  class: com.example.owner.HandleOwnerNotFound
```

```java
public class HandleOwnerNotFound {
  public void handle(@Parameter OwnerNotFoundException ex,
      ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<String>> response) {
    response.send(new ResponseEntity<>(ex.getMessage(), HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND));
  }
}
```

### Step wiring

Each top-level YAML entry is a developer-chosen step name; the first is the entry
point. `class:` names the function. **Give each function class exactly one public
method** — several public methods fail at start-up unless every reference adds
`method:`.

- `next: <step>` — run that step afterwards. This step's return value arrives there
  as `@Parameter T`.
- `outputs: { <name>: <step> }` — conditional branches. Declare a
  `@FunctionalInterface` parameter annotated `@Flow("<name>")` and call it to take the
  branch; not calling it short-circuits.

### Function parameters

Declare only what the step needs; they resolve by role:

- `@PathVariable`, `@RequestParam`, `@RequestBody` — Spring MVC annotations work.
- Spring beans (repositories, mappers, services) — injected by type as normal.
- `ObjectResponse<T>` (`net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse`) — send the response with
  `response.send(dto)`. This is how a step responds; wrap as
  `ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<T>>` to set status explicitly.
- `@Parameter T` (`net.officefloor.plugin.section.clazz.Parameter`) — the previous
  step's return value, a `@Flow` argument, or a thrown escalation.

### Passing state between steps — `Out<T>` / `@Val`

Steps do not call each other. Beyond the single `@Parameter` hand-off, publish state
into a variable (`net.officefloor.plugin.variable`):

- Producer declares `Out<T>` and calls `set(...)`; consumer declares `@Val T`.
- Matching is **by type** — two variables of the same type in one pipeline need a
  `@Qualifier` annotation to disambiguate.
- `@Val` yields the same object the producer stored, **not a copy** — so an `Apply`
  step mutates the entity in place and later steps see the change.

### Naming

Verb plus entity: `Load<E>` (fetch by path variable, publishes `Out<E>`, throws when
absent) · `Build<E>` (construct from body) · `Validate<E>` (bind and validate the body,
publish it) · `Apply<E>` (mutate) · `Save<E>` · `Delete<E>` · `RespondWith<E>` (200) ·
`RespondWith<E>Created` (201) · `RespondWithNoContent` (204).

Keep DTOs at the edges — request body in at the first step, response DTO out at the
responder. Steps in between work with entities.

### Request body and validation

- The HTTP body can be read only once: **only one step per pipeline may bind
  `@RequestBody`**. A second binding fails at runtime. When later steps need it, the
  first step publishes it as a variable.
- `@Valid` runs before that step's method body, so step order decides when validation
  happens. Put the validating step first — otherwise a missing id returns 404 before an
  invalid body can return 400.

### Transactions

`govern: [ transaction ]` for writes, `govern: [ readonly-transaction ]` for reads,
listed on **every** step it covers. Both are provided by the starter. Governance spans
the pipeline, so the request commits once at the end.

### Errors

Functions throw; handlers respond. The exception must be **checked** (`extends
Exception`) so it appears in the `throws` clause. Put the handler in
`officefloor/escalation/<fully.qualified.ExceptionClass>.yml`, taking the exception as
`@Parameter` and responding via `ObjectResponse`. Matching is most-specific-first;
anything unmatched falls through to Spring `@RestControllerAdvice`.

### Security

Guard a whole endpoint file with a Spring Security SpEL expression:

```yaml
composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"
```

# OfficeFloor REST wiring

Domain REST endpoints are declared here as OfficeFloor YAML, served by the
`officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` inside the Spring Boot host. Put them under `rest/api/` so
their paths start with `/api/` — `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend; a non-`/api/`
path returns the SPA's `index.html` instead of your endpoint. Directory nesting maps to path
segments, so `rest/api/owners.GET.yml` → `GET /api/owners`. Each route is its own file:

```
# officefloor/rest/api/<path>.GET.yml   (or .POST.yml, {param}.GET.yml, ...)
service:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.<SomeLogic>   # a class with a service(...) method
```

The logic class's `service(...)` method takes injected dependencies (Spring `@Service` beans, the
data layer) and a `net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse<T>` to send the response.

(The `/actuator/health` readiness endpoint is Spring-side — Actuator — not an OfficeFloor route.)
=== status.POST.yml
     1	# POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/status — move a claim to a new status (body
     2	# {status, user, review, reason}): DRAFT to OPEN, OPEN to SETTLED, DRAFT, OPEN or PENDING to VOID,
     3	# and SETTLED to VOID by a steward within 7 days of its settling (its status log's SETTLED date); DRAFT
     4	# to DELETED (deleted: it counts nowhere), and DELETED back to DRAFT (restored) only on the sheet's today it
     5	# was deleted on (its status log's last DELETED date).
     6	# A clerk (any user not assigned steward) settling a claim whose due is above the sheet's clerk limit
     7	# sends it to PENDING instead. A steward, or the approver of the claim's person, reviews a PENDING claim (review true): status SETTLED approves
     8	# it (not by the user who opened it or last edited it), status OPEN with a reason rejects it. Refused (400) for any
     9	# other change, when the sheet's permission matrix (perm-open, perm-settle, perm-void; by default a
    10	# clerk or a steward) does not allow the user's role to open, settle or void, when settling or approving a claim with no proofs whose due is above the proof threshold
    11	# in force on its date, when opening a claim with an empty note whose due is above the note threshold
    12	# in force on its date (both checked before the clerk limit, so it never goes to PENDING), when the user who opened the claim or last edited it (claim form or amount entry) tries to settle or approve it, when the claim is not on
    13	# the sheet, or when its due-by falls in a closed period, or when opening a DRAFT whose due-by falls in a period
    14	# with a cap while its person already has that many OPEN or PENDING claims due in it; nothing is stored then. Opening records the
    15	# user as the claim's opened-by; a claim whose due is above the review threshold in force on its date goes to REVIEW (no
    16	# number yet, CLAIM_REVIEW) instead of OPEN, and only a steward's review (status OPEN, review true) moves it on: CLAIM_REVIEWED,
    17	# then CLAIM_OPENED with its number. A REVIEW claim may otherwise only be voided.
    18	# A stored change is recorded in the audit file as CLAIM_OPENED,
    19	# CLAIM_PENDING, CLAIM_SETTLED, CLAIM_APPROVED, CLAIM_REJECTED, CLAIM_VOIDED, CLAIM_DELETED or CLAIM_RESTORED (with reversed=<the
    20	# frozen figure> when a SETTLED claim is voided). While the sheet has void reasons, a void needs one of
    21	# them as its reason (refused otherwise); it is kept on the claim and CLAIM_VOIDED ends with reason=<it>.
    22	# A settle may name a date (on, yyyy-MM-dd): its due is then frozen as the claim stood at the end of that date (the
    23	# as-of view, the date standing in for the sheet's today), and CLAIM_SETTLED ends with on=<date>; refused when the
    24	# date is after the sheet's today or the claim (or its person) was not on the sheet then.

=== {claimId}.PUT.yml
1:# PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId} — edit a draft claim's amount, date, note, ref, tags and the
2:# claim it corrects (body as an add; a correction is checked as on an add). Refused (400) like an add, when the claim is not on the sheet, when it is not a DRAFT
3:# (an open claim is voided and added anew instead), or
4:# when another user has locked it by opening its editor, when its due-by (fixed when it was added, so left as it is by an edit) falls in a closed period, or when its new date is after the date
5:# its person is retired from, or when its ref is one another claim on the sheet carries, or when it has lines and the edit types another amount than theirs; nothing is stored then.
6:# A stored change records the user as the claim's edited-by (who may then not settle or approve it), releases the claim's lock and is recorded in the audit file as CLAIM_EDITED; a refused one records nothing.

1:# POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/defer — defer an OPEN claim (body {until, user}) until a
2:# date after the sheet's today. Until the sheet's today reaches that date the claim counts in no total,
3:# is not overdue, cannot be settled and is left unbound by a statement; from that day on it is an OPEN
4:# claim like any other. Refused (400) when the date does not parse or is not after today, the claim is
5:# not OPEN or not on the sheet, or its due-by falls in a closed period; nothing is stored then. A stored
6:# deferral is recorded in the audit file as CLAIM_DEFERRED.

1:# POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/settle-part — part-settle an OPEN claim (body {amount, user}): the

4:# claim may not settle it) and the proof rule are judged on the original claim; the new claim's opener is the user,
5:# who may still settle it. Refused (400), storing and auditing nothing, when the split or the settle would be

4:# date and note, the next number, opened by the user, split-from the claim's number and due by its date

content.content:
=== bulk-open
1:# POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/bulk-open — open the selected claims together (body {claimIds, user}).
2:# Each selected claim that can be opened (a DRAFT on the sheet, not due by a date in a closed period, nor in a capped period its person already has that many OPEN or
3:# PENDING claims in, with a note or a due not above the note threshold in force on
4:# its date) is
5:# opened and numbered in list order — people by their positions, a person's claims
6:# newest first — and recorded as CLAIM_OPENED, as a single open is; each that cannot is refused and
7:# left as it is. Answers {opened, refused}. Refused (400) only when no claim is selected.
9:  class: claim.ValidateBulkOpen
12:  class: claim.OpenClaims
16:  class: claim.RespondWithBulkOpen
=== bulk-settle
1:# POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/bulk-settle — settle the selected claims together (body {claimIds, user}).
2:# Each selected claim is settled in list order — people by their positions, a person's
3:# claims newest first — by exactly the rules of a single settle by the user, and recorded as a single
4:# settle is (CLAIM_SETTLED, or CLAIM_PENDING for a clerk above the clerk limit, which counts as
5:# settled). All or nothing: when a single settle would refuse any of them, none is settled, every one
6:# counts as refused and nothing is written; otherwise BATCH_SETTLED follows the claims' own records.
7:# Answers {settled, refused}. Refused (400) only when no claim is selected.
9:  class: claim.ValidateBulkSettle
12:  class: claim.SettleClaims
16:  class: claim.RespondWithBulkSettle
=== bulk-void
1:# POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/bulk-void — void the selected claims together (body {claimIds, user, reason}).
2:# Each selected claim is voided in list order — people by their positions, a person's claims newest
3:# first — by exactly the rules of a single void by the user with the reason (a void reason needed while
4:# the sheet has any), and recorded as a single void is (CLAIM_VOIDED, then how it moved the sheet's
5:# figures). Each that a single void would refuse, or that is not on the sheet, is refused and left as it
6:# is, writing nothing. Answers {voided, refused}. Refused (400) only when no claim is selected.
8:  class: claim.ValidateBulkVoid
11:  class: claim.VoidClaims
15:  class: claim.RespondWithBulkVoid
=== bulk-redate
1:# POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/bulk-redate — re-date the selected claims together (body {claimIds, date, user}).
2:# Each selected claim is re-dated in list order — people by their positions, a person's claims newest
3:# first — by exactly the rules of a single re-dating by the user (who may, which statuses, closed periods,
4:# retirement), and recorded as a single re-dating is (CLAIM_REDATED and its rollup lines); each that a single
5:# re-dating would refuse is refused and left as it is. Answers {redated, refused}. Refused (400) only when no
6:# claim is selected or the date does not parse.
8:  class: claim.ValidateBulkRedate
11:  class: claim.RedateClaims
15:  class: claim.RespondWithBulkRedate
=== bulk-reassign
1:# POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/bulk-reassign — move the selected claims to another person together (body
2:# {claimIds, to, user}, `to` the person's id). Each selected claim is moved in list order — people by their
3:# positions, a person's claims newest first — by exactly the rules of a single move by the user
4:# (who may, which statuses, closed periods, retirement), and recorded as a single move is (CLAIM_REASSIGNED
5:# and its rollup lines); each that a single move would refuse is refused and left as it is. Answers
6:# {reassigned, refused}. Refused (400) only when no claim or no person is chosen.
8:  class: claim.ValidateBulkReassign
11:  class: claim.ReassignClaims
15:  class: claim.RespondWithBulkReassign

content.content:
=== import-openings
1:# POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/import-openings — add opening balances (body: {text, user}). Each line is
2:# name,period,amount: a person on the sheet by name or alias, a period on the sheet and an amount of two
3:# decimals, 0.00 or more. Every line is checked first; refused (400), storing nothing and recording nothing,
4:# when any line fails or there is no line. Otherwise each amount is added to the person's opening balance for
5:# the period (part of their carried figure for it) and recorded as OPENING_SET. Answers {set}.
7:  class: opening.ValidateOpeningImport
11:  class: opening.SaveOpeningImport
15:  class: opening.RespondWithOpeningImport
=== paste-claims
1:# POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/paste-claims — add a DRAFT claim per pasted line, in order (body: {text,
2:# user}). Each line is name,amount,date,note: the name must be on the sheet (ignoring case and the
3:# spaces around it), the date may be blank for the sheet's today, the note may hold commas or be
4:# absent. A note ending in " #<ref>" gives the claim that external reference (not part of the note);
5:# a reference used on the sheet or earlier in the paste, without regard to case, refuses the paste. Every line is first checked with the claim form's rules; refused (400), storing nothing and
6:# recording nothing, when any line fails or there is no line. A line naming a person, date and note
7:# that match one of their claims as they stood before the paste (void and deleted ones aside; never a
8:# claim an earlier line added) updates the newest such DRAFT instead: edited to the line's amount
9:# (CLAIM_EDITED when it changes); a line whose matches include no DRAFT refuses the paste. Then, in
10:# paste order, each claim is added (CLAIM_ADDED, as a single add is) or edited, and opened by the user
11:# exactly as the open button would (numbered, CLAIM_OPENED with the rollup lines). Any refusal the add,
12:# edit or open would give refuses the whole paste, storing and recording nothing. Answers {added}: how
13:# many lines went through.
15:  class: paste.ValidatePaste
19:  class: paste.SavePasted
23:  class: paste.RespondWithPaste
=== quick-add
1:# POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/quick-add — add a DRAFT claim for a person by name (body: {name, amount,
2:# user}), dated the sheet's today with an empty note. A name not on the sheet (ignoring case and the
3:# spaces around it) adds the person first, with the sheet's default grade (A unless set). The person form's and the claim form's
4:# rules apply: refused (400), storing nothing and recording nothing, when the name is empty, the
5:# amount is not valid, the due-by the claim would be fixed with (its date plus
6:# the terms it would get) falls in a closed period, or the named person is retired
7:# from a date before it. The whole quick add is one
8:# change: the person is added only once the claim has passed every check.
9:# Records PERSON_ADDED (and its ROLLUP) for a new person, then CLAIM_ADDED.
11:  class: quick.ValidateQuickAdd
14:  class: quick.CheckQuickAddPeriod
18:  class: quick.FindOrAddPerson
22:  class: rollup.SnapshotRollup
26:  class: claim.SaveClaimAdded
30:  class: claim.AuditClaimAdded
34:  class: claim.RespondWithClaim
=== templates
1:# POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/templates — saves a claim template (body: {name, amount, note, user}), name and
2:# note trimmed; saving a name again replaces its amount and note. A blank name, an amount the claim form
3:# would refuse, or a viewer is refused (400) and nothing is stored. Recorded as TEMPLATE_SAVED.
5:  class: template.ValidateTemplate
8:  class: template.SaveTemplate
12:  class: template.AuditTemplateSaved
16:  class: template.RespondWithTemplate
=== plans/generate
1:# POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/plans/generate — for every plan on the sheet in the order they were added,
2:# a DRAFT claim of its amount, dated that day with an empty note, for every plan date up to its end and the
3:# sheet's today that it has made none for yet, by the claim form's rules: a date the form refuses is
4:# skipped and tried again next time. Each is recorded as CLAIM_ADDED. Answers {generated}. Refused (400)
5:# on an archived sheet. A viewer makes none: answers {generated: 0}, storing and recording nothing.
7:  class: plan.ValidatePlanGenerate
10:  class: plan.GeneratePlanClaims
14:  class: plan.RespondWithPlanGenerate
=== people/{personId}/plans
1:# POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/plans — add a plan to a person (body: {amount, start, every,
2:# end, user}): a DRAFT claim of the amount for every plan date (the start, then every N days) up to the end,
3:# made by POST plans/generate. The amount is a number with up to two decimals, every a whole number of at
4:# least 1, the dates yyyy-MM-dd (a blank start the sheet's today). Refused (400), storing nothing, when any
5:# is not, the end is before the start, or the person is not on the sheet. Recorded as PLAN_ADDED.

=== people/{personId}/template-claims
1:# POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/template-claims — add a DRAFT claim to a person from a
2:# template (body: {template, user}): the template's amount and note as they are now, with no date (so

1:# POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/claims — add a claim to a person (body: {amount,
2:# date, note, user, corrects, ref}). The amount is required: a number with up to two decimals. A
3:# negative amount is a correction: corrects must name, by number, a SETTLED claim of the same person

6:# retired from a date before it, or when its ref (spaces around it removed; blank for none) is one
7:# another claim on the sheet carries, compared without regard to case.
8:# A stored change is recorded in the audit file as CLAIM_ADDED; a refused one records nothing.

# POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/hold — add a hold on a person (body: {from, to, user}):
# a blank from-date takes the sheet's today, a blank to-date has no end. A person may have several
# holds over time; a hold ends on its to-date. Only their OPEN (or PENDING) claims dated within a
# hold are left out of the live totals (their own, the sheet's, a period's); a claim bound by a
# statement stays in them whatever its date, and their SETTLED claims always do. Refused (400),
# storing nothing, when a date is not valid, the to-date is before the from-date, or the person is
# not on the sheet. A stored hold is recorded in the audit file as PERSON_HELD, followed by how it
# moved the figures.
